newsitem.title: USA: SOCCER-GALAXY TIE MLS PLAYOFF SERIES WITH SAN JOSE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GALAXY TIE MLS PLAYOFF SERIES WITH SAN JOSE.

text.p: The Los Angeles Galaxy scored twice in the final six minutes to pull out a 2-0 win over the San Jose Clash on Sunday and tie their Major Soccer League conference semifinal series.

Robin Fraser scored for the Western Conference champions in the 84th minute and Ecuadoran Eduardo Hurtado added an insurance goal in the final minute to force a deciding game in the semifinal series on Wednesday.

The Clash won the opener 1-0 in San Jose on Thursday on Tayt Ianni's first goal of the season as he converted a header off U.S. international forward Eric Wynalda's corner kick past goalkeeper Jorge Campos. Wynalda, who was ejected in the 87th minute for his second yellow card, will not play Wednesday.
All four playoff series are tied at one game apiece, with all deciding matches on Wednesday.

In the other Western Conference semifinal series, the host Dallas Burn remained alive against the Kansas City Wiz after a 2-1 home victory on Sunday. Dante Washington's header in the 32nd minute broke a 1-1.

Midfielder Jason Kreis, who was not expected to play because of a dislocated left elbow, scored for the Burn in the fifth minute as Preki, who put in the game-winner on Thursday, tied it in the 30th minute.
Preki's goal in the 89th minute lifted the Wiz to a 3-2 victory over the Burn in Kansas City in front of 4,446 fans, the smallest crowd of the league's inaugural season.

After one-time Scottish international Mo Johnson connected for Kansas City, Dallas grabbed a 2-1 lead on goals by Gerell Elliott and Chad Ashton midway through the first half. But Matt McKeon tied it with 11 minutes remaining.
The Tampa Bay Mutiny (20-12), who finished with the best record in the league, will meet the Columbus Crew in the final game of an Eastern Conference semifinal series.
The Mutiny won the first game 2-0 last Wednesday as Roy Lassiter, the regular-season scoring champion, struck twice in the final 14 minutes.

The Crew tied the series in Tampa on Saturday when Brian McBride broke a 1-1 tie in the 58th minute en route to a 2-1 triumph. Adrian Paz scored 26 seconds into the match for the Crew, but Lassiter equalised.
D.C. United tied their Eastern Conference series with the New York/New Jersey MetroStars in Washington, D.C. on Friday night as Bolivian Marco Etcheverry scored the lone goal in a 1-0 win.
The MetroStars won the first game in an 11-round marathon shootout 6-5 after playing to a 2-2 tie in regulation on Tuesday.
Colombian Antony De Avila and Venezuelan Giovanni Savarese, a second-half sub, scored for the hosts, El Salvadoran Raul Arce Diaz and Jaime Moreno for United.

The MetroStars prevailed in a controversial shootout as sweeper and team captain Peter Vermes converted the game-winner, although United coach Bruce Arena claimed that Vermes shot out of turn. United protested, but the league ruled that the result stood.
